Joses
JO-seez
n. (proper, a brother of the Lord; a Greek form of Joseph)
Greek Ioses, a form of Joseph. The Authorized Version uses it of more than one man, chiefly of a brother of our Lord named in the two lists the townsmen of Nazareth recited when they took offence at him.

Biblical Definition

The men of Nazareth answered his teaching with his family tree: “Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?” (Matthew 13:55). Mark records the same objection with the trade attached to Jesus himself: “Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him” (Mark 6:3). Joses is named second in both lists. At the cross and the tomb a Mary is identified by him: “And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid” (Mark 15:47). The brethren of the Lord did not believe on him during his ministry, and after the resurrection they are found in the upper room with the disciples and with Mary his mother, continuing with one accord in prayer and supplication.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as a Greek form of Joseph, borne by a brother of the Lord named in Matthew 13 and Mark 6.

expand to see more

BRETHREN, n. pl. Plural of brother; used in the solemn and scriptural style.

CARPENTER, n. An artificer who works in timber; a framer and builder of houses and of ships.

OFFEND, v.t. To displease; to make angry; to affront; in Scripture, to cause to stumble.

NAZARETH, n. A town of Galilee, the home of Joseph and Mary and the place of our Lord's upbringing.

UNBELIEF, n. Infidelity; disbelief of divine revelation; in Scripture, the sin of not receiving Christ.

Key Scripture

Matthew 13:55 — "Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?"

Mark 6:3 — "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him."

Mark 15:47 — "And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid."

John 7:5 — "For neither did his brethren believe in him."

Modern Corruption

Familiarity is mistaken for knowledge: the men who knew our Lord's trade, mother and brothers by name concluded from that very knowledge that he could be nothing more, and were offended at him.

expand to see more

Mark 6:3 is a warning aimed at everyone raised near the things of God. The townsmen were not ignorant; they were the best informed people in Galilee about Jesus of Nazareth. They knew his trade, his mother, his four brothers by name and his sisters by sight, and the conclusion they drew from all that information was and they were offended at him. Knowing a great deal about Christ, having grown up with the facts, is not the same as receiving him, and it can be the very thing that prevents it. He did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

The encouragement is what became of the brethren. John 7:5 states it without softening: For neither did his brethren believe in him. Joses is in that number. And after the resurrection, Acts 1:14 finds the apostles continuing in prayer “with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren”. James, named first in both lists, became a pillar of the Jerusalem church and wrote an epistle in which he calls himself a servant of the Lord Jesus Christ rather than his brother. Long unbelief in a family is not the end of the account; the risen Christ changed the minds of the men who grew up in his house.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek Ioses (G2500), Joses, a form of Joseph; adelphos (G80), a brother; tekton (G5045), a carpenter or builder; skandalizo (G4624), to cause to stumble.

expand to see more

Greek Ioses (G2500) — Joses; a Greek form of the Hebrew Joseph.

Greek adelphos (G80) — a brother; used of James, Joses, Simon and Judas.

Greek tekton (G5045) — a worker in wood or stone, a carpenter; our Lord's trade.

Greek skandalizo (G4624) — to put a stumbling block before; they were offended at him.

Greek homothumadon (G3661) — with one accord; the brethren in the upper room afterwards.

Usage

"“His brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?” — the town's objection."

"“And they were offended at him” — the conclusion from knowing too much."

"“Neither did his brethren believe in him” — and afterwards they did."
